# T7.03: B pictures through VideoToolbox

(The other two T7.03 reports are about an earlier, abandoned approach to registration: CoreMedia code signing.)

## What changed

`vt/nvencvt.c` reorders frames when the client allows it and is not real time; details in docs/vt-encoder.md "B pictures".
The encoder side (`enc_submit_ex`, B setups for H.264 and HEVC from the Linux driver trace) was already done (M13 era,
commits 339e845, e3fdbf0, 1ff42a6). `tools/vtencfile.m` got `VT_REORDER`, `VT_KEYINT`, `VT_SRC` (raw NV12 input, looped)
and checks every sample's time stamps (decode times increase, no decode after presentation).

## Results (guest, RTX 4090, 1920x1080 crowd_run, 300 frames = the 60-frame clip looped)

At 12 Mbit/s CBR (`VT_BITRATE=12000000`), luma PSNR against the source, VideoToolbox frame rate:

| | P only, fast controls | P only, quality | 2 B, fast | 2 B, quality (default when not real time) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| H.264 High CABAC | 28.47 dB, 230 fps | 28.67 dB, 223 fps | 28.82 dB, 199 fps | **29.08 dB, 185 fps** |
| HEVC Main | 28.94 dB, 184 fps | (same: H.264 only) | **29.19 dB**, 199 fps | |

- Constant QP, key interval 0 and 25: ffmpeg decodes all four streams without errors, worst frame within 0.6 dB of the
  average (no broken pictures across the POC LSB wrap at 128 frames); 12 sync samples for interval 25.
- AVAssetWriter (`tools/avwrite`, 1, 2, 7 and 120 frames, H.264 and HEVC): every frame reads back and matches.
- OBS 32.2.2, "B-frames" on, H.264 and HEVC: 60 fps, 0 decode errors.
- Encoder stats: for a B picture "call" now includes the time it waited for its anchor (~one frame period per B).

## Lessons

- Replacing the signed `libnvencvt.dylib` in the driver bundle with `cp` over the old file killed every Metal app
  ("Code Signature Invalid" in dyld, OBS crash-looped): macOS caches the signature per vnode. Copy to a new name,
  `codesign -f -s -`, `chown root:wheel`, `chmod 755`, then `mv` over it.
- vtencfile stalled for up to 35 s at random in `NSLog` (logd); it prints with `fprintf` now.
- In the guest, screencapture exits 1 while the display sleeps; `vm/tahoe/guest-shot.sh` wakes it first.
